Hi Lauren —

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. The team is excited about the latency and cost numbers you showed. We’re close to internal alignment, but two items came up in procurement that I want to flag before we proceed: 1) MicroBurst needs a single-seat operator bundle for our pilot environment (short term) instead of the standard 5-seat minimum; 2) procurement is asking whether Redwood can provide a one-time onboarding credit to offset cloud egress costs during the first 90 days (they want this documented on the SOW).

Attached is our SOW draft (MicroBurst_SOW_v1.pdf) and a simple run-rate estimate for the pilot. High-level ask: 40% one-off credit applied to the first month’s committed usage and allowance to purchase a 1-seat operator license for the pilot term.

Can you confirm whether either is plausible? If so, we’ll push legal to accept the SOW and move to signature.

—Claire

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai

Subject: Fwd: MicroBurst pilot: request for one-off onboarding credit + 1-seat pilot bundle (need VP/CFO review)

Marissa / Aditya / Jonas —

Forwarding Claire’s note and the SOW. TL;DR: MicroBurst (early-stage infra SaaS) wants: 1) a one-time 40% onboarding credit applied to month 1 committed usage to offset egress; 2) allow them to buy a 1-seat operator bundle for the 90-day pilot (we’d restore the 5-seat minimum at renewal).

Why I’m asking for sign-off: MicroBurst is a fast-moving prospect with solid technical fit (we validated perf in the PoC). The total dollar impact of the credit is modest (~$12k gross in month 1) but it’s a non-recurring concession that sets a slightly different precedent on seat minimums. I recommend approving on a conditional basis with these guardrails:
- Credit recorded as a one-time onboarding credit on the SOW (not a permanent list-price change)
- Credit capped (explicit $ amount in SOW) and tied to usage evidence in first invoice
- 1-seat pilot bundle valid for the pilot term only; automatic reversion to 5-seat minimum on renewal
- Require legal to include a clause that customer may not combine this concession with other promotional programs

Requested action: Aditya — please confirm finance OK for a capped one-time credit (I’ve attached the pricing sheet). Marissa — can you confirm commercial/partner implications and whether we need VP-level approval beyond your signoff? Jonas — optional; ask CS to prepare a one-line ops addendum.

Attachments: redwood_pricing_model_v3.xlsx, MicroBurst_SOW_v1.pdf

Thanks,
Lauren

From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-02T15:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: MicroBurst pilot: request for one-off onboarding credit + 1-seat pilot bundle (need VP/CFO review)

Lauren / team —

Thanks for the clear summary. I’ve reviewed the numbers and redwood_pricing_model_v3.xlsx. Recommendation: approve a capped, one-time onboarding credit not to exceed $15,000 (aligns with Lauren’s estimate and keeps FY impact contained). Approve the 1-seat operator pilot bundle for the 90-day term with the strict reversion clause on renewal. Conditions:

- Credit to be documented as a non-recurring line item on the SOW and tracked in billing as a contra-revenue item
- Legal to add a clause preventing stacking with other discounts/promotions and requiring usage evidence for credit application
- Sales to record this as an exception in the CRM with the deal_id MB-2027-0421 and copy Finance on the first invoice evidence email

Marissa — if you’re comfortable with acceptance on these terms, I’ll sign off from Finance. If you want VP-level written approval, please indicate and I’ll escalate.
